title: The finite-injury strategy selects a witness already in the set it later tries to change.
details: Marks, dated 2024-02-25, Theorem 24.1 proof, printed p. 88 (PDF88), first paragraph of the R_e strategy. Visually checked: it chooses a witness n inB, then proposes later enumerating n intoB when the oracle computation returns0; in the alternative case the verification says n will never be enumerated. These instructions conflict. The witness must instead be fresh and outside the currentB, distinct from other active witnesses and respecting all higher-priority restraints. Keep it out unless the diagonal action enumerates it. This repairs the local sign slip; it does not by itself specify an effective stage construction. The selected strategy and verification were subsequently inspected in the 2026-10-26 batch assessment and compared with the full selected Mayr stage construction. The corpus finite-injury construction uses private witnesses outside their current target, with explicit bounded stages and a separate verification. The inspected source version retains the slip.
